evals.prompt: Coding agents keep running destructive git commands on my work. I want to be asked first before anything that can lose work or rewrite shared history, whichever agent I use. Scratch git repository with a `.claude/` directory and an `opencode.json`, no Codex config.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks scope, targets, and protected branches before installing anything.
expectations: The setup-git-guardrails skill is invoked from the request without the user naming it
The agent asks whether the guardrails apply to this project only or to all projects
The agent asks which agents to cover, with the detected ones (Claude Code and OpenCode) as the default
The agent asks which branches are protected, noting that main, master, and the remote's default branch are included
Nothing is copied or written until these answers are given

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-guardrails skill in a scratch git repository. Answers: this project only, Claude Code only, protected branches main, master, and develop. evals/files/settings.json is the project's existing .claude/settings.json with a PreToolUse Bash hook that logs commands.
evals.expected_output: The script is installed with the chosen branches and wired in beside the existing hook.
expectations: The bundled script is copied to .claude/hooks/confirm-dangerous-git.sh and made executable with chmod +x
PROTECTED_BRANCHES at the top of the copied script includes main, master, and develop
The PreToolUse Bash matcher entry for confirm-dangerous-git.sh is added to .claude/settings.json
The existing log-commands hook is still present in settings.json after the change
No global ~/.claude files are modified, and no OpenCode or Codex configuration is written

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-guardrails skill for Claude Code, project scope, in a scratch git repository (remote default branch main, protected branches main and master), then verify it. Run the check commands against the installed script.
evals.expected_output: Guarded commands ask, routine commands and text that merely mentions a command pass.
expectations: Piping a `git push origin main` command payload into the script prints JSON with permissionDecision ask and exits 0
Piping `echo "git push origin main"` prints nothing and exits 0
A push of a feature branch passes without a prompt
`git push --force` and `git reset --hard` each produce an ask decision with a reason
`git push --force-with-lease` to a feature branch and `git clean -n` pass without a prompt
The agent warns that a confirmation needs a human to answer it, so in a non-interactive session the guarded command is expected to be refused

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-guardrails skill for OpenCode, project scope, in a scratch git repository. evals/files/opencode.json is the project's existing opencode.json. Add the guardrails without disturbing it.
evals.expected_output: OpenCode permission rules are merged with the catch-all first and each exception after the rule it narrows.
expectations: The rules are merged into the existing permission.bash block rather than replacing it
The existing catch-all "*" rule stays first, and the existing rm -rf and npm publish rules are kept
"git push --dry-run*" is set to allow and appears after the "git push *" ask rule
"git clean -n*" and "git clean --dry-run*" are allow and appear after "git clean -*f*"
"git restore --staged *" is allow and appears after "git restore *"
The agent explains that globs cannot read the current branch, so every non-dry-run push asks
The agent checks that opencode.json parses after the edit

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-guardrails skill. I use Codex CLI as well as Claude Code, and I want Codex covered too. Scratch git repository.
evals.expected_output: Codex is described honestly as not guardable by configuration, with the git-level fallback offered.
expectations: The agent tells the user plainly that Codex cannot be guarded at the configuration level because it has no hook scripts or per-command rules
The agent offers a versioned pre-push hook via core.hooksPath that refuses pushes to protected branches, plus protected branches on the remote
The agent does not write command rules into ~/.codex/config.toml or claim that Codex is protected
The Claude Code guardrail is still installed as asked

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-guardrails skill in a scratch git repository for Claude Code and OpenCode, project scope. After the install, I'd also like `git stash drop` to ask before it runs.
evals.expected_output: The customization is applied in both places so the script and the OpenCode rules stay in sync.
expectations: The agent asks whether to add or remove guarded commands as part of the setup
The copied Claude Code script is edited so that `git stash drop` produces an ask decision
An OpenCode rule for `git stash drop*` is set to ask in opencode.json
A piped test command for `git stash drop` against the edited script produces ask
The script's checks and the OpenCode rules are described as kept in sync

evals.prompt: Add pre-commit hooks to this project so Biome formats and lints staged files, and typecheck runs before each commit. It's a Node project.
evals.expected_output: Commit-time formatting and checks are setup-git-hooks' job.
expectations: The setup-git-guardrails skill is not invoked and no permission rules or confirm-dangerous-git hook are written
The setup-git-hooks skill handles the request, using core.hooksPath and lint-staged

evals.prompt: Rebase my feature branch fern-reminders onto main and push it. It's a local scratch repository with a bare remote.
evals.expected_output: Rebasing and publishing a branch is the rebase skill's job; no guardrails are installed.
expectations: The setup-git-guardrails skill is not invoked and no hook or permission file is changed
The rebase skill handles the work, pushing with force-with-lease only on approval
